00.b1e67b5a89:
<n>8:2</n> Dómine, Dóminus noster, * quam admirábile est nomen tuum in univérsa terra!
<n>8:2</n> Quóniam eleváta est magnificéntia tua, * super cælos.
<n>8:3</n> Ex ore infántium et lacténtium perfecísti laudem propter inimícos tuos, * ut déstruas inimícum et ultórem.
<n>8:4</n> Quóniam vidébo cælos tuos, ópera digitórum tuórum: * lunam et stellas, quæ tu fundásti.
<n>8:5</n> Quid est homo quod memor es eius? * aut fílius hóminis, quóniam vísitas eum?
<n>8:6</n> Minuísti eum paulo minus ab Ángelis, glória et honóre coronásti eum: * et constituísti eum super ópera mánuum tuárum.
<n>8:8</n> Ómnia subiecísti sub pédibus eius, * oves et boves univérsas: ínsuper et pécora campi.
<n>8:9</n> Vólucres cæli, et pisces maris, * qui perámbulant sémitas maris.
<n>8:10</n> Dómine, Dóminus noster, * quam admirábile est nomen tuum in univérsa terra!
00.22ccb0113c:
<n>8:2</n> O Lord our Lord, * how admirable is thy name in the whole earth!
<n>8:2</n> For thy magnificence is elevated * above the heavens.
<n>8:3</n> Out of the mouth of infants and of sucklings thou hast perfected praise, because of thy enemies, * that thou mayst destroy the enemy and the avenger.
<n>8:4</n> For I will behold thy heavens, the works of thy fingers: * the moon and the stars which thou hast founded.
<n>8:5</n> What is man that thou art mindful of him? * or the son of man that thou visitest him?
<n>8:6</n> Thou hast made him a little less than the angels, thou hast crowned him with glory and honour: * and hast set him over the works of thy hands.
<n>8:8</n> Thou hast subjected all things under his feet, * all sheep and oxen: moreover the beasts also of the fields.
<n>8:9</n> The birds of the air, and the fishes of the sea, * that pass through the paths of the sea.
<n>8:10</n> O Lord our Lord, * how admirable is thy name in all the earth!
00.fe79c3969e:
<n>3:57</n> Benedícite, ómnia ópera Dómini, Dómino: * laudáte et superexaltáte eum in sǽcula.
<n>3:58</n> Benedícite, Ángeli Dómini, Dómino: * benedícite, cæli, Dómino.
<n>3:59</n> Benedícite, aquæ omnes, quæ super cælos sunt, Dómino: * benedícite, omnes virtútes Dómini, Dómino.
<n>3:60</n> Benedícite, sol et luna, Dómino: * benedícite, stellæ cæli, Dómino.
<n>3:61</n> Benedícite, omnis imber et ros, Dómino: * benedícite, omnes spíritus Dei, Dómino.
<n>3:62</n> Benedícite, ignis et æstus, Dómino: * benedícite, frigus et æstus, Dómino.
<n>3:63</n> Benedícite, rores et pruína, Dómino: * benedícite, gelu et frigus, Dómino.
<n>3:64</n> Benedícite, glácies et nives, Dómino: * benedícite, noctes et dies, Dómino.
<n>3:65</n> Benedícite, lux et ténebræ, Dómino: * benedícite, fúlgura et nubes, Dómino.
<n>3:66</n> Benedícat terra Dóminum: * laudet et superexáltet eum in sǽcula.
<n>3:67</n> Benedícite, montes et colles, Dómino: * benedícite, univérsa germinántia in terra, Dómino.
<n>3:68</n> Benedícite, fontes, Dómino: * benedícite, mária et flúmina, Dómino.
<n>3:69</n> Benedícite, cete, et ómnia, quæ movéntur in aquis, Dómino: * benedícite, omnes vólucres cæli, Dómino.
<n>3:70</n> Benedícite, omnes béstiæ et pécora, Dómino: * benedícite, fílii hóminum, Dómino.
<n>3:71</n> Benedícat Israël Dóminum: * laudet et superexáltet eum in sǽcula.
<n>3:72</n> Benedícite, sacerdótes Dómini, Dómino: * benedícite, servi Dómini, Dómino.
<n>3:73</n> Benedícite, spíritus, et ánimæ iustórum, Dómino: * benedícite, sancti, et húmiles corde, Dómino.
<n>3:74</n> Benedícite, Ananía, Azaría, Mísaël, Dómino: * laudáte et superexaltáte eum in sǽcula.
<n>3:75</n> <n>(Fit reverentia:)</n> Benedicámus Patrem et Fílium cum Sancto Spíritu: * laudémus et superexaltémus eum in sǽcula.
<n>3:56</n> Benedíctus es, Dómine, in firmaménto cæli: * et laudábilis, et gloriósus, et superexaltátus in sǽcula.
00.439cfbefdc:
<n>3:57</n> All ye works of the Lord, bless the Lord: * praise and exalt him above all for ever.
<n>3:58</n> O ye angels of the Lord, bless the Lord: * O ye heavens, bless the Lord:
<n>3:59</n> O all ye waters that are above the heavens, bless the Lord: * O all ye powers of the Lord, bless the Lord.
<n>3:60</n> O ye sun and moon, bless the Lord: * O ye stars of heaven, bless the Lord.
<n>3:61</n> O every shower and dew, bless ye the Lord: * O all ye spirits of God, bless the Lord.
<n>3:62</n> O ye fire and heat, bless the Lord: * O ye cold and heat, bless the Lord.
<n>3:63</n> O ye dews and hoar frosts, bless the Lord: * O ye frost and cold, bless the Lord.
<n>3:64</n> O ye ice and snow, bless the Lord: * O ye nights and days, bless the Lord.
<n>3:65</n> O ye light and darkness, bless the Lord: * O ye lightnings and clouds, bless the Lord.
<n>3:66</n> O let the earth bless the Lord: * let it praise and exalt him above all for ever.
<n>3:67</n> O ye mountains and hills, bless the Lord: * O all ye things that spring up in the earth, bless the Lord.
<n>3:68</n> O ye fountains, bless the Lord: * O ye seas and rivers, bless the Lord.
<n>3:69</n> O ye whales, and all that move in the waters, bless the Lord: * O all ye fowls of the air, bless the Lord.
<n>3:70</n> O all ye beasts and cattle, bless the Lord: * O ye sons of men, bless the Lord.
<n>3:71</n> O let Israel bless the Lord: * let them praise and exalt him above all for ever.
<n>3:72</n> O ye priests of the Lord, bless the Lord: * O ye servants of the Lord, bless the Lord.
<n>3:73</n> O ye spirits and souls of the just, bless the Lord: * O ye holy and humble of heart, bless the Lord.
<n>3:74</n> O Ananias, Azarias, and Misael, bless ye the Lord: * praise and exalt him above all for ever.
<n>3:75</n> <n>(Bow head)</n> Let us bless the Father and the Son, with the Holy Ghost; * let us praise and exalt him above all for ever.
<n>3:56</n> Blessed art thou, O Lord, in the firmament of heaven: * and worthy of praise, and glorious for ever.
00.a84ba42878:
<n>1:68</n> Benedíctus ✠ Dóminus, Deus Israël: * quia visitávit, et fecit redemptiónem plebis suæ:
<n>1:69</n> Et eréxit cornu salútis nobis: * in domo David, púeri sui.
<n>1:70</n> Sicut locútus est per os sanctórum, * qui a sǽculo sunt, prophetárum eius:
<n>1:71</n> Salútem ex inimícis nostris, * et de manu ómnium, qui odérunt nos.
<n>1:72</n> Ad faciéndam misericórdiam cum pátribus nostris: * et memorári testaménti sui sancti.
<n>1:73</n> Iusiurándum, quod iurávit ad Ábraham patrem nostrum, * datúrum se nobis:
<n>1:74</n> Ut sine timóre, de manu inimicórum nostrórum liberáti, * serviámus illi.
<n>1:75</n> In sanctitáte, et iustítia coram ipso, * ómnibus diébus nostris.
<n>1:76</n> Et tu, puer, Prophéta Altíssimi vocáberis: * præíbis enim ante fáciem Dómini, paráre vias eius:
<n>1:77</n> Ad dandam sciéntiam salútis plebi eius: * in remissiónem peccatórum eórum:
<n>1:78</n> Per víscera misericórdiæ Dei nostri: * in quibus visitávit nos, óriens ex alto:
<n>1:79</n> Illumináre his, qui in ténebris, et in umbra mortis sedent: * ad dirigéndos pedes nostros in viam pacis.
00.b647a6b6c9:
<n>1:68</n> Blessed be the Lord ✠ God of Israel; * because he hath visited and wrought the redemption of his people:
<n>1:69</n> And hath raised up an horn of salvation to us, * in the house of David his servant:
<n>1:70</n> As he spoke by the mouth of his holy Prophets, * who are from the beginning:
<n>1:71</n> Salvation from our enemies, * and from the hand of all that hate us:
<n>1:72</n> To perform mercy to our fathers, * and to remember his holy testament,
<n>1:73</n> The oath, which he swore to Abraham our father, * that he would grant to us,
<n>1:74</n> That being delivered from the hand of our enemies, * we may serve him without fear,
<n>1:75</n> In holiness and justice before him, * all our days.
<n>1:76</n> And thou, child, shalt be called the prophet of the Highest: * for thou shalt go before the face of the Lord to prepare his ways:
<n>1:77</n> To give knowledge of salvation to his people, * unto the remission of their sins:
<n>1:78</n> Through the bowels of the mercy of our God, * in which the Orient from on high hath visited us:
<n>1:79</n> To enlighten them that sit in darkness, and in the shadow of death: * to direct our feet into the way of peace.
00.a228cea5a8:
<n>1:46</n> Magníficat ✠ * ánima mea Dóminum.
<n>1:47</n> Et exsultávit spíritus meus: * in Deo, salutári meo.
<n>1:48</n> Quia respéxit humilitátem ancíllæ suæ: * ecce enim ex hoc beátam me dicent omnes generatiónes.
<n>1:49</n> Quia fecit mihi magna qui potens est: * et sanctum nomen eius.
<n>1:50</n> Et misericórdia eius, a progénie in progénies: * timéntibus eum.
<n>1:51</n> Fecit poténtiam in brácchio suo: * dispérsit supérbos mente cordis sui.
<n>1:52</n> Depósuit poténtes de sede: * et exaltávit húmiles.
<n>1:53</n> Esuriéntes implévit bonis: * et dívites dimísit inánes.
<n>1:54</n> Suscépit Israël púerum suum: * recordátus misericórdiæ suæ.
<n>1:55</n> Sicut locútus est ad patres nostros: * Ábraham, et sémini eius in sǽcula.
00.83742356bc:
<n>1:46</n> My soul ✠ * doth magnify the Lord.
<n>1:47</n> And my spirit hath rejoiced * in God my Saviour.
<n>1:48</n> Because he hath regarded the humility of his handmaid; * for behold from henceforth all generations shall call me blessed.
<n>1:49</n> Because he that is mighty, hath done great things to me; * and holy is his name.
<n>1:50</n> And his mercy is from generation unto generations, * to them that fear him.
<n>1:51</n> He hath shewed might in his arm: * he hath scattered the proud in the conceit of their heart.
<n>1:52</n> He hath put down the mighty from their seat, * and hath exalted the humble.
<n>1:53</n> He hath filled the hungry with good things; * and the rich he hath sent empty away.
<n>1:54</n> He hath received Israel his servant, * being mindful of his mercy:
<n>1:55</n> As he spoke to our fathers, * to Abraham and to his seed for ever.
00.79d0f0e10a:
<n>4:2</n> Cum invocárem exaudívit me Deus iustítiæ meæ: * in tribulatióne dilatásti mihi.
<n>4:2</n> Miserére mei, * et exáudi oratiónem meam.
<n>4:3</n> Fílii hóminum, úsquequo gravi corde? * ut quid dilígitis vanitátem, et quǽritis mendácium?
<n>4:4</n> Et scitóte quóniam mirificávit Dóminus sanctum suum: * Dóminus exáudiet me cum clamávero ad eum.
<n>4:5</n> Irascímini, et nolíte peccáre: * quæ dícitis in córdibus vestris, in cubílibus vestris compungímini.
<n>4:6</n> Sacrificáte sacrifícium iustítiæ, et speráte in Dómino. * Multi dicunt: Quis osténdit nobis bona?
<n>4:7</n> Signátum est super nos lumen vultus tui, Dómine: * dedísti lætítiam in corde meo.
<n>4:8</n> A fructu fruménti, vini, et ólei sui * multiplicáti sunt.
<n>4:9</n> In pace in idípsum * dórmiam, et requiéscam;
<n>4:10</n> Quóniam tu, Dómine, singuláriter in spe * constituísti me.
00.a47be6b05e:
<n>4:2</n> When I called upon him, the God of my justice heard me: * when I was in distress, thou hast enlarged me.
<n>4:2</n> Have mercy on me: * and hear my prayer.
<n>4:3</n> O ye sons of men, how long will you be dull of heart? * Why do you love vanity, and seek after lying?
<n>4:4</n> Know ye also that the Lord hath made his holy one wonderful: * the Lord will hear me when I shall cry unto him.
<n>4:5</n> Be ye angry, and sin not: * the things you say in your hearts, be sorry for them upon your beds.
<n>4:6</n> Offer up the sacrifice of justice, and trust in the Lord: * many say, Who sheweth us good things?
<n>4:7</n> The light of thy countenance, O Lord, is signed upon us: * thou hast given gladness in my heart.
<n>4:8</n> By the fruit of their corn, their wine, and oil, * they are multiplied.
<n>4:9</n> In peace in the selfsame * I will sleep, and I will rest:
<n>4:10</n> For thou, O Lord, singularly * hast settled me in hope.
00.f0c002767a:
<n>2:29</n> Nunc dimíttis ✠ servum tuum, Dómine, * secúndum verbum tuum in pace:
<n>2:30</n> Quia vidérunt óculi mei * salutáre tuum,
<n>2:31</n> Quod parásti * ante fáciem ómnium populórum,
<n>2:32</n> Lumen ad revelatiónem géntium, * et glóriam plebis tuæ Israël.
00.89b4b60b5f:
<n>2:29</n> Now ✠ thou dost dismiss thy servant, O Lord, * according to thy word in peace;
<n>2:30</n> Because my eyes have seen * thy salvation,
<n>2:31</n> Which thou hast prepared * before the face of all peoples:
<n>2:32</n> A light to the revelation of the Gentiles, * and the glory of thy people Israel.
00.d64a793782:
<n>5:2</n> Verba mea áuribus pércipe, Dómine, * intéllege clamórem meum.
<n>5:3</n> Inténde voci oratiónis meæ, * Rex meus et Deus meus.
<n>5:4</n> Quóniam ad te orábo: * Dómine, mane exáudies vocem meam.
<n>5:5</n> Mane astábo tibi et vidébo: * quóniam non Deus volens iniquitátem tu es.
<n>5:6</n> Neque habitábit iuxta te malígnus: * neque permanébunt iniústi ante óculos tuos.
<n>5:7</n> Odísti omnes, qui operántur iniquitátem: * perdes omnes, qui loquúntur mendácium.
<n>5:7</n> Virum sánguinum et dolósum abominábitur Dóminus: * ego autem in multitúdine misericórdiæ tuæ.
<n>5:8</n> Introíbo in domum tuam: * adorábo ad templum sanctum tuum in timóre tuo.
<n>5:9</n> Dómine, deduc me in iustítia tua: * propter inimícos meos dírige in conspéctu tuo viam meam.
<n>5:10</n> Quóniam non est in ore eórum véritas: * cor eórum vanum est.
<n>5:11</n> Sepúlcrum patens est guttur eórum, linguis suis dolóse agébant, * iúdica illos, Deus.
<n>5:11</n> Décidant a cogitatiónibus suis, secúndum multitúdinem impietátum eórum expélle eos, * quóniam irritavérunt te, Dómine.
<n>5:12</n> Et læténtur omnes, qui sperant in te, * in ætérnum exsultábunt: et habitábis in eis.
<n>5:12</n> Et gloriabúntur in te omnes, qui díligunt nomen tuum, * quóniam tu benedíces iusto.
<n>5:13</n> Dómine, ut scuto bonæ voluntátis tuæ * coronásti nos.
00.02ee367e2e:
<n>5:2</n> Give ear, O Lord, to my words * understand my cry.
<n>5:3</n> Hearken to the voice of my prayer, * O my King and my God.
<n>5:4</n> For to thee will I pray: * O Lord, in the morning thou shalt hear my voice.
<n>5:5</n> In the morning I will stand before thee, and will see: * because thou art not a God that willest iniquity.
<n>5:6</n> Neither shall the wicked dwell near thee: * nor shall the unjust abide before thy eyes.
<n>5:7</n> Thou hatest all the workers of iniquity: * thou wilt destroy all that speak a lie.
<n>5:7</n> The bloody and the deceitful man the Lord will abhor. * But as for me in the multitude of thy mercy,
<n>5:8</n> I will come into thy house; * I will worship towards thy holy temple, in thy fear.
<n>5:9</n> Conduct me, O Lord, in thy justice: * because of my enemies, direct my way in thy sight.
<n>5:10</n> For there is no truth in their mouth: * their heart is vain.
<n>5:11</n> Their throat is an open sepulchre: they dealt deceitfully with their tongues: * judge them, O God.
<n>5:11</n> Let them fall from their devices: according to the multitude of their wickednesses cast them out: * for they have provoked thee, O Lord.
<n>5:12</n> But let all them be glad that hope in thee: * they shall rejoice for ever, and thou shalt dwell in them.
<n>5:12</n> And all they that love thy name shall glory in thee: * For thou wilt bless the just.
<n>5:13</n> O Lord, thou hast crowned us, * as with a shield of thy good will.
00.239f5c450a:
<n>6:2</n> Dómine, ne in furóre tuo árguas me, * neque in ira tua corrípias me.
<n>6:3</n> Miserére mei, Dómine, quóniam infírmus sum: * sana me, Dómine, quóniam conturbáta sunt ossa mea.
<n>6:4</n> Et ánima mea turbáta est valde: * sed tu, Dómine, úsquequo?
<n>6:5</n> Convértere, Dómine, et éripe ánimam meam: * salvum me fac propter misericórdiam tuam.
<n>6:6</n> Quóniam non est in morte qui memor sit tui: * in inférno autem quis confitébitur tibi?
<n>6:7</n> Laborávi in gémitu meo, lavábo per síngulas noctes lectum meum: * lácrimis meis stratum meum rigábo.
<n>6:8</n> Turbátus est a furóre óculus meus: * inveterávi inter omnes inimícos meos.
<n>6:9</n> Discédite a me, omnes, qui operámini iniquitátem: * quóniam exaudívit Dóminus vocem fletus mei.
<n>6:10</n> Exaudívit Dóminus deprecatiónem meam, * Dóminus oratiónem meam suscépit.
<n>6:11</n> Erubéscant, et conturbéntur veheménter omnes inimíci mei: * convertántur et erubéscant valde velóciter.
00.44e5e213e3:
<n>6:2</n> Lord, rebuke me not in thy indignation, * nor chastise me in thy wrath.
<n>6:3</n> Have mercy on me, O Lord, for I am weak: * heal me, O Lord, for my bones are troubled.
<n>6:4</n> And my soul is troubled exceedingly: * but thou, O Lord, how long?
<n>6:5</n> Turn to me, O Lord, and deliver my soul: * O save me for thy mercy’s sake.
<n>6:6</n> For there is no one in death, that is mindful of thee: * and who shall confess to thee in hell?
<n>6:7</n> I have laboured in my groanings, every night I will wash my bed: * I will water my couch with my tears.
<n>6:8</n> My eye is troubled through indignation: * I have grown old amongst all my enemies.
<n>6:9</n> Depart from me, all ye workers of iniquity: * for the Lord hath heard the voice of my weeping.
<n>6:10</n> The Lord hath heard my supplication: * the Lord hath received my prayer.
<n>6:11</n> Let all my enemies be ashamed, and be very much troubled: * let them be turned back, and be ashamed very speedily.
00.f43b57c9ae:
<n>7:2</n> Dómine, Deus meus, in te sperávi: * salvum me fac ex ómnibus persequéntibus me, et líbera me.
<n>7:3</n> Nequándo rápiat ut leo ánimam meam, * dum non est qui rédimat, neque qui salvum fáciat.
<n>7:4</n> Dómine, Deus meus, si feci istud, * si est iníquitas in mánibus meis:
<n>7:5</n> Si réddidi retribuéntibus mihi mala, * décidam mérito ab inimícis meis inánis.
<n>7:6</n> Persequátur inimícus ánimam meam, et comprehéndat, et concúlcet in terra vitam meam, * et glóriam meam in púlverem dedúcat.
<n>7:7</n> Exsúrge, Dómine, in ira tua: * et exaltáre in fínibus inimicórum meórum.
<n>7:7</n> Et exsúrge, Dómine, Deus meus, in præcépto quod mandásti: * et synagóga populórum circúmdabit te.
<n>7:8</n> Et propter hanc in altum regrédere: * Dóminus iúdicat pópulos.
<n>7:9</n> Iúdica me, Dómine, secúndum iustítiam meam, * et secúndum innocéntiam meam super me.
<n>7:10</n> Consumétur nequítia peccatórum, et díriges iustum, * scrutans corda et renes, Deus.
<n>7:11</n> Iustum adiutórium meum a Dómino, * qui salvos facit rectos corde.
<n>7:12</n> Deus iudex iustus, fortis, et pátiens: * numquid iráscitur per síngulos dies?
<n>7:13</n> Nisi convérsi fuéritis, gládium suum vibrábit: * arcum suum teténdit, et parávit illum.
<n>7:14</n> Et in eo parávit vasa mortis: * sagíttas suas ardéntibus effécit.
<n>7:15</n> Ecce, partúriit iniustítiam: * concépit dolórem, et péperit iniquitátem.
<n>7:16</n> Lacum apéruit, et effódit eum: * et íncidit in fóveam quam fecit.
<n>7:17</n> Convertétur dolor eius in caput eius: * et in vérticem ipsíus iníquitas eius descéndet.
<n>7:18</n> Confitébor Dómino secúndum iustítiam eius: * et psallam nómini Dómini altíssimi.
00.af1b65fc25:
<n>7:2</n> O Lord my God, in thee have I put my trust: * save me from all them that persecute me, and deliver me.
<n>7:3</n> Lest at any time he seize upon my soul like a lion, * while there is no one to redeem me, nor to save.
<n>7:4</n> O Lord my God, if I have done this thing, * if there be iniquity in my hands:
<n>7:5</n> If I have rendered to them that repaid me evils, * let me deservedly fall empty before my enemies.
<n>7:6</n> Let the enemy pursue my soul, and take it, and tread down my life on the earth, * and bring down my glory to the dust.
<n>7:7</n> Rise up, O Lord, in thy anger: * and be thou exalted in the borders of my enemies.
<n>7:7</n> And arise, O Lord my God, in the precept which thou hast commanded: * and a congregation of people shall surround thee.
<n>7:8</n> And for their sakes return thou on high. * The Lord judgeth the people.
<n>7:9</n> Judge me, O Lord, according to my justice, * and according to my innocence in me.
<n>7:10</n> The wickedness of sinners shall be brought to nought: and thou shalt direct the just: * the searcher of hearts and reins is God.
<n>7:11</n> Just is my help from the Lord: * who saveth the upright of heart.
<n>7:12</n> God is a just judge, strong and patient: * is he angry every day?
<n>7:13</n> Except you will be converted, he will brandish his sword: * he hath bent his bow, and made it ready.
<n>7:14</n> And in it he hath prepared the instruments of death, * he hath made ready his arrows for them that burn.
<n>7:15</n> Behold he hath been in labour with injustice; * he hath conceived sorrow, and brought forth iniquity.
<n>7:16</n> He hath opened a pit and dug it: * and he is fallen into the hole he made.
<n>7:17</n> His sorrow shall be turned on his own head: * and his iniquity shall come down upon his crown.
<n>7:18</n> I will give glory to the Lord according to his justice: * and will sing to the name of the Lord the most High.
00.cd311610f7:
<n>1:1</n> Beátus vir, qui non ábiit in consílio impiórum, et in via peccatórum non stetit, * et in cáthedra pestiléntiæ non sedit:
<n>1:2</n> Sed in lege Dómini volúntas eius, * et in lege eius meditábitur die ac nocte.
<n>1:3</n> Et erit tamquam lignum, quod plantátum est secus decúrsus aquárum, * quod fructum suum dabit in témpore suo:
<n>1:3</n> Et fólium eius non défluet: * et ómnia quæcúmque fáciet, prosperabúntur.
<n>1:4</n> Non sic ímpii, non sic: * sed tamquam pulvis, quem próicit ventus a fácie terræ.
<n>1:5</n> Ídeo non resúrgent ímpii in iudício: * neque peccatóres in concílio iustórum.
<n>1:6</n> Quóniam novit Dóminus viam iustórum: * et iter impiórum períbit.
00.377711dfcd:
<n>1:1</n> Blessed is the man who hath not walked in the counsel of the ungodly, nor stood in the way of sinners, * nor sat in the chair of pestilence.
<n>1:2</n> But his will is in the law of the Lord, * and on his law he shall meditate day and night.
<n>1:3</n> And he shall be like a tree which is planted near the running waters, * which shall bring forth its fruit, in due season.
<n>1:3</n> And his leaf shall not fall off: * and all whatsoever he shall do shall prosper.
<n>1:4</n> Not so the wicked, not so: * but like the dust, which the wind driveth from the face of the earth.
<n>1:5</n> Therefore the wicked shall not rise again in judgment: * nor sinners in the council of the just.
<n>1:6</n> For the Lord knoweth the way of the just: * and the way of the wicked shall perish.
00.9c05588177:
<n>2:1</n> Quare fremuérunt gentes: * et pópuli meditáti sunt inánia?
<n>2:2</n> Astitérunt reges terræ, et príncipes convenérunt in unum * advérsus Dóminum, et advérsus Christum eius.
<n>2:3</n> Dirumpámus víncula eórum: * et proiciámus a nobis iugum ipsórum.
<n>2:4</n> Qui hábitat in cælis, irridébit eos: * et Dóminus subsannábit eos.
<n>2:5</n> Tunc loquétur ad eos in ira sua, * et in furóre suo conturbábit eos.
<n>2:6</n> Ego autem constitútus sum Rex ab eo super Sion montem sanctum eius, * prǽdicans præcéptum eius.
<n>2:7</n> Dóminus dixit ad me: * Fílius meus es tu, ego hódie génui te.
<n>2:8</n> Póstula a me, et dabo tibi gentes hereditátem tuam, * et possessiónem tuam términos terræ.
<n>2:9</n> Reges eos in virga férrea, * et tamquam vas fíguli confrínges eos.
<n>2:10</n> Et nunc, reges, intellégite: * erudímini, qui iudicátis terram.
<n>2:11</n> Servíte Dómino in timóre: * et exsultáte ei cum tremóre.
<n>2:12</n> Apprehéndite disciplínam, nequándo irascátur Dóminus, * et pereátis de via iusta.
<n>2:13</n> Cum exárserit in brevi ira eius: * beáti omnes qui confídunt in eo.
00.7ba7fd590b:
<n>2:1</n> Why have the Gentiles raged, * and the people devised vain things?
<n>2:2</n> The kings of the earth stood up, and the princes met together, * against the Lord and against his Christ.
<n>2:3</n> Let us break their bonds asunder: * and let us cast away their yoke from us.
<n>2:4</n> He that dwelleth in heaven shall laugh at them: * and the Lord shall deride them.
<n>2:5</n> Then shall he speak to them in his anger, * and trouble them in his rage.
<n>2:6</n> But I am appointed king by him over Sion his holy mountain, * preaching his commandment.
<n>2:7</n> The Lord hath said to me: * Thou art my son, this day have I begotten thee.
<n>2:8</n> Ask of me, and I will give thee the Gentiles for thy inheritance, * and the utmost parts of the earth for thy possession.
<n>2:9</n> Thou shalt rule them with a rod of iron, * and shalt break them in pieces like a potter’s vessel.
<n>2:10</n> And now, O ye kings, understand: * receive instruction, you that judge the earth.
<n>2:11</n> Serve ye the Lord with fear: * and rejoice unto him with trembling.
<n>2:12</n> Embrace discipline, lest at any time the Lord be angry, * and you perish from the just way.
<n>2:13</n> When his wrath shall be kindled in a short time, * blessed are all they that trust in him.
00.c04ac7cadc:
<n>3:2</n> Dómine, quid multiplicáti sunt qui tríbulant me? * multi insúrgunt advérsum me.
<n>3:3</n> Multi dicunt ánimæ meæ: * Non est salus ipsi in Deo eius.
<n>3:4</n> Tu autem, Dómine, suscéptor meus es, * glória mea, et exáltans caput meum.
<n>3:5</n> Voce mea ad Dóminum clamávi: * et exaudívit me de monte sancto suo.
<n>3:6</n> Ego dormívi, et soporátus sum: * et exsurréxi, quia Dóminus suscépit me.
<n>3:7</n> Non timébo míllia pópuli circumdántis me: * exsúrge, Dómine, salvum me fac, Deus meus.
<n>3:8</n> Quóniam tu percussísti omnes adversántes mihi sine causa: * dentes peccatórum contrivísti.
<n>3:9</n> Dómini est salus: * et super pópulum tuum benedíctio tua.
00.88fb122d10:
<n>3:2</n> Why, O Lord, are they multiplied that afflict me? * many are they who rise up against me.
<n>3:3</n> Many say to my soul: * There is no salvation for him in his God.
<n>3:4</n> But thou, O Lord art my protector, * my glory, and the lifter up of my head.
<n>3:5</n> I have cried to the Lord with my voice: * and he hath heard me from his holy hill.
<n>3:6</n> I have slept and taken my rest: * and I have risen up, because the Lord hath protected me.
<n>3:7</n> I will not fear thousands of the people, surrounding me: * arise, O Lord; save me, O my God.
<n>3:8</n> For thou hast struck all them who are my adversaries without cause: * thou hast broken the teeth of sinners.
<n>3:9</n> Salvation is of the Lord: * and thy blessing is upon thy people.
00.1aaf03a99e:
<n>9:2</n> Confitébor tibi, Dómine, in toto corde meo: * narrábo ómnia mirabília tua.
<n>9:3</n> Lætábor et exsultábo in te: * psallam nómini tuo, Altíssime.
<n>9:4</n> In converténdo inimícum meum retrórsum: * infirmabúntur, et períbunt a fácie tua.
<n>9:5</n> Quóniam fecísti iudícium meum et causam meam: * sedísti super thronum, qui iúdicas iustítiam.
<n>9:6</n> Increpásti gentes, et périit ímpius: * nomen eórum delésti in ætérnum, et in sǽculum sǽculi.
<n>9:7</n> Inimíci defecérunt frámeæ in finem: * et civitátes eórum destruxísti.
<n>9:7</n> Périit memória eórum cum sónitu: * et Dóminus in ætérnum pérmanet.
<n>9:8</n> Parávit in iudício thronum suum: * et ipse iudicábit orbem terræ in æquitáte, iudicábit pópulos in iustítia.
<n>9:10</n> Et factus est Dóminus refúgium páuperi: * adiútor in opportunitátibus, in tribulatióne.
<n>9:11</n> Et sperent in te qui novérunt nomen tuum: * quóniam non dereliquísti quæréntes te, Dómine.
00.d90c99b20f:
<n>9:2</n> I will give praise to thee, O Lord, with my whole heart: * I will relate all thy wonders.
<n>9:3</n> I will be glad and rejoice in thee: * I will sing to thy name, O thou most high.
<n>9:4</n> When my enemy shall be turned back: * they shall be weakened and perish before thy face.
<n>9:5</n> For thou hast maintained my judgment and my cause: * thou hast sat on the throne, who judgest justice.
<n>9:6</n> Thou hast rebuked the Gentiles, and the wicked one hath perished: * thou hast blotted out their name for ever and ever.
<n>9:7</n> The swords of the enemy have failed unto the end: * and their cities thou hast destroyed.
<n>9:7</n> Their memory hath perished with a noise. * But the Lord remaineth for ever.
<n>9:8</n> He hath prepared his throne in judgment: * And he shall judge the world in equity, he shall judge the people in justice.
<n>9:10</n> And the Lord is become a refuge for the poor: * a helper in due time in tribulation.
<n>9:11</n> And let them trust in thee who know thy name: * for thou hast not forsaken them that seek thee, O Lord.
00.6fe618985b:
<n>9:12</n> Psállite Dómino, qui hábitat in Sion: * annuntiáte inter gentes stúdia eius:
<n>9:13</n> Quóniam requírens sánguinem eórum recordátus est: * non est oblítus clamórem páuperum.
<n>9:14</n> Miserére mei, Dómine: * vide humilitátem meam de inimícis meis.
<n>9:15</n> Qui exáltas me de portis mortis, * ut annúntiem omnes laudatiónes tuas in portis fíliæ Sion.
<n>9:16</n> Exsultábo in salutári tuo: * infíxæ sunt gentes in intéritu, quem fecérunt.
<n>9:16</n> In láqueo isto, quem abscondérunt, * comprehénsus est pes eórum.
<n>9:17</n> Cognoscétur Dóminus iudícia fáciens: * in opéribus mánuum suárum comprehénsus est peccátor.
<n>9:18</n> Convertántur peccatóres in inférnum, * omnes gentes quæ obliviscúntur Deum.
<n>9:19</n> Quóniam non in finem oblívio erit páuperis: * patiéntia páuperum non períbit in finem.
<n>9:20</n> Exsúrge, Dómine, non confortétur homo: * iudicéntur gentes in conspéctu tuo.
<n>9:21</n> Constítue, Dómine, legislatórem super eos: * ut sciant gentes quóniam hómines sunt.
00.7453d5d4f6:
<n>9:12</n> Sing ye to the Lord, who dwelleth in Sion: * declare his ways among the Gentiles.
<n>9:13</n> For requiring their blood he hath remembered them: * he hath not forgotten the cry of the poor.
<n>9:14</n> Have mercy on me, O Lord: * see my humiliation which I suffer from my enemies.
<n>9:15</n> Thou that liftest me up from the gates of death, * that I may declare all thy praises in the gates of the daughter of Sion.
<n>9:16</n> I will rejoice in thy salvation: * the Gentiles have stuck fast in the destruction which they have prepared.
<n>9:16</n> Their foot hath been taken * in the very snare which they hid.
<n>9:17</n> The Lord shall be known when he executeth judgments: * the sinner hath been caught in the works of his own hands.
<n>9:18</n> The wicked shall be turned into hell, * all the nations that forget God.
<n>9:19</n> For the poor man shall not be forgotten to the end: * the patience of the poor shall not perish for ever.
<n>9:20</n> Arise, O Lord, let not man be strengthened: * let the Gentiles be judged in thy sight.
<n>9:21</n> Appoint, O Lord, a lawgiver over them: * that the Gentiles may know themselves to be but men.
00.dad2b93f32:
<n>9:22</n> Ut quid, Dómine, recessísti longe, * déspicis in opportunitátibus, in tribulatióne?
<n>9:23</n> Dum supérbit ímpius, incénditur pauper: * comprehendúntur in consíliis quibus cógitant.
<n>9:24</n> Quóniam laudátur peccátor in desidériis ánimæ suæ: * et iníquus benedícitur.
<n>9:25</n> Exacerbávit Dóminum peccátor, * secúndum multitúdinem iræ suæ non quæret.
<n>9:26</n> Non est Deus in conspéctu eius: * inquinátæ sunt viæ illíus in omni témpore.
<n>9:26</n> Auferúntur iudícia tua a fácie eius: * ómnium inimicórum suórum dominábitur.
<n>9:27</n> Dixit enim in corde suo: * Non movébor a generatióne in generatiónem sine malo.
<n>9:28</n> Cuius maledictióne os plenum est, et amaritúdine, et dolo: * sub lingua eius labor et dolor.
<n>9:29</n> Sedet in insídiis cum divítibus in occúltis: * ut interfíciat innocéntem.
<n>9:30</n> Óculi eius in páuperem respíciunt: * insidiátur in abscóndito, quasi leo in spelúnca sua.
<n>9:30</n> Insidiátur ut rápiat páuperem: * rápere páuperem, dum áttrahit eum.
<n>9:31</n> In láqueo suo humiliábit eum: * inclinábit se, et cadet, cum dominátus fúerit páuperum.
<n>9:32</n> Dixit enim in corde suo: Oblítus est Deus, * avértit fáciem suam ne vídeat in finem.
00.942dcd5084:
<n>9:22</n> Why, O Lord, hast thou retired afar off? * why dost thou slight us in our wants, in the time of trouble?
<n>9:23</n> Whilst the wicked man is proud, the poor is set on fire: * they are caught in the counsels which they devise.
<n>9:24</n> For the sinner is praised in the desires of his soul: * and the unjust man is blessed.
<n>9:25</n> The sinner hath provoked the Lord, * according to the multitude of his wrath he will not seek him.
<n>9:26</n> God is not before his eyes: * his ways are filthy at all times.
<n>9:26</n> Thy judgments are removed from his sight: * he shall rule over all his enemies.
<n>9:27</n> For he hath said in his heart: * I shall not be moved from generation to generation, and shall be without evil.
<n>9:28</n> His mouth is full of cursing, and of bitterness, and of deceit: * under his tongue are labour and sorrow.
<n>9:29</n> He sitteth in ambush with the rich, in private places, * that he may kill the innocent.
<n>9:30</n> His eyes are upon the poor man: * he lieth in wait, in secret, like a lion in his den.
<n>9:30</n> He lieth in ambush, that he may catch the poor man: * so catch the poor, whilst he draweth him to him.
<n>9:31</n> In his net he will bring him down, * he will crouch and fall, when he shall have power over the poor.
<n>9:32</n> For he hath said in his heart: God hath forgotten, * he hath turned away his face, not to see to the end.
00.3a77a0e01d:
<n>9:33</n> Exsúrge, Dómine Deus, exaltétur manus tua: * ne obliviscáris páuperum.
<n>9:34</n> Propter quid irritávit ímpius Deum? * dixit enim in corde suo: Non requíret.
<n>9:35</n> Vides quóniam tu labórem et dolórem consíderas: * ut tradas eos in manus tuas.
<n>9:35</n> Tibi derelíctus est pauper: * órphano tu eris adiútor.
<n>9:36</n> Cóntere brácchium peccatóris et malígni: * quærétur peccátum illíus, et non inveniétur.
<n>9:37</n> Dóminus regnábit in ætérnum, et in sǽculum sǽculi: * períbitis, gentes, de terra illíus.
<n>9:38</n> Desidérium páuperum exaudívit Dóminus: * præparatiónem cordis eórum audívit auris tua.
<n>9:39</n> Iudicáre pupíllo et húmili, * ut non appónat ultra magnificáre se homo super terram.
00.b8fed76636:
<n>9:33</n> Arise, O Lord God, let thy hand be exalted: * forget not the poor.
<n>9:34</n> Wherefore hath the wicked provoked God? * for he hath said in his heart: He will not require it.
<n>9:35</n> Thou seest it, for thou considerest labour and sorrow: * that thou mayst deliver them into thy hands.
<n>9:35</n> To thee is the poor man left: * thou wilt be a helper to the orphan.
<n>9:36</n> Break thou the arm of the sinner and of the malignant: * his sin shall be sought, and shall not be found.
<n>9:37</n> The Lord shall reign to eternity, yea, for ever and ever: * ye Gentiles shall perish from his land.
<n>9:38</n> The Lord hath heard the desire of the poor: * thy ear hath heard the preparation of their heart.
<n>9:39</n> To judge for the fatherless and for the humble, * that man may no more presume to magnify himself upon earth.
00.959f5c1b9f:
<n>7:2</n> Dómine, Deus meus, in te sperávi: * salvum me fac ex ómnibus persequéntibus me, et líbera me.
<n>7:3</n> Nequándo rápiat ut leo ánimam meam, * dum non est qui rédimat, neque qui salvum fáciat.
<n>7:4</n> Dómine, Deus meus, si feci istud, * si est iníquitas in mánibus meis:
<n>7:5</n> Si réddidi retribuéntibus mihi mala, * décidam mérito ab inimícis meis inánis.
<n>7:6</n> Persequátur inimícus ánimam meam, et comprehéndat, et concúlcet in terra vitam meam, * et glóriam meam in púlverem dedúcat.
<n>7:7</n> Exsúrge, Dómine, in ira tua: * et exaltáre in fínibus inimicórum meórum.
<n>7:7</n> Et exsúrge, Dómine, Deus meus, in præcépto quod mandásti: * et synagóga populórum circúmdabit te.
<n>7:8</n> Et propter hanc in altum regrédere: * Dóminus iúdicat pópulos.
<n>7:9</n> Iúdica me, Dómine, secúndum iustítiam meam, * et secúndum innocéntiam meam super me.
<n>7:10</n> Consumétur nequítia peccatórum, et díriges iustum, * scrutans corda et renes, Deus.
00.cb1570b3af:
<n>7:2</n> O Lord my God, in thee have I put my trust: * save me from all them that persecute me, and deliver me.
<n>7:3</n> Lest at any time he seize upon my soul like a lion, * while there is no one to redeem me, nor to save.
<n>7:4</n> O Lord my God, if I have done this thing, * if there be iniquity in my hands:
<n>7:5</n> If I have rendered to them that repaid me evils, * let me deservedly fall empty before my enemies.
<n>7:6</n> Let the enemy pursue my soul, and take it, and tread down my life on the earth, * and bring down my glory to the dust.
<n>7:7</n> Rise up, O Lord, in thy anger: * and be thou exalted in the borders of my enemies.
<n>7:7</n> And arise, O Lord my God, in the precept which thou hast commanded: * and a congregation of people shall surround thee.
<n>7:8</n> And for their sakes return thou on high. * The Lord judgeth the people.
<n>7:9</n> Judge me, O Lord, according to my justice, * and according to my innocence in me.
<n>7:10</n> The wickedness of sinners shall be brought to nought: and thou shalt direct the just: * the searcher of hearts and reins is God.
00.e19dcd71a8:
<n>7:11</n> Iustum adiutórium meum a Dómino, * qui salvos facit rectos corde.
<n>7:12</n> Deus iudex iustus, fortis, et pátiens: * numquid iráscitur per síngulos dies?
<n>7:13</n> Nisi convérsi fuéritis, gládium suum vibrábit: * arcum suum teténdit, et parávit illum.
<n>7:14</n> Et in eo parávit vasa mortis: * sagíttas suas ardéntibus effécit.
<n>7:15</n> Ecce, partúriit iniustítiam: * concépit dolórem, et péperit iniquitátem.
<n>7:16</n> Lacum apéruit, et effódit eum: * et íncidit in fóveam quam fecit.
<n>7:17</n> Convertétur dolor eius in caput eius: * et in vérticem ipsíus iníquitas eius descéndet.
<n>7:18</n> Confitébor Dómino secúndum iustítiam eius: * et psallam nómini Dómini altíssimi.
00.03a1a17f47:
<n>7:11</n> Just is my help from the Lord: * who saveth the upright of heart.
<n>7:12</n> God is a just judge, strong and patient: * is he angry every day?
<n>7:13</n> Except you will be converted, he will brandish his sword: * he hath bent his bow, and made it ready.
<n>7:14</n> And in it he hath prepared the instruments of death, * he hath made ready his arrows for them that burn.
<n>7:15</n> Behold he hath been in labour with injustice; * he hath conceived sorrow, and brought forth iniquity.
<n>7:16</n> He hath opened a pit and dug it: * and he is fallen into the hole he made.
<n>7:17</n> His sorrow shall be turned on his own head: * and his iniquity shall come down upon his crown.
<n>7:18</n> I will give glory to the Lord according to his justice: * and will sing to the name of the Lord the most High.
00.0361e85d9f:
<n>2:1</n> Exsultávit cor meum in Dómino, * et exaltátum est cornu meum in Deo meo.
<n>2:2</n> Dilatátum est os meum super inimícos meos: * quia lætáta sum in salutári tuo.
<n>2:3</n> Non est sanctus, ut est Dóminus: neque enim est álius extra te, * et non est fortis sicut Deus noster.
<n>2:4</n> Nolíte multiplicáre loqui sublímia, * gloriántes:
<n>2:5</n> Recédant vétera de ore vestro: quia Deus scientiárum, Dóminus est, * et ipsi præparántur cogitatiónes.
<n>2:6</n> Arcus fórtium superátus est, * et infírmi accíncti sunt róbore.
<n>2:7</n> Repléti prius, pro pánibus se locavérunt: * et famélici saturáti sunt.
<n>2:8</n> Donec stérilis péperit plúrimos: * et quæ multos habébat fílios, infirmáta est.
<n>2:9</n> Dóminus mortíficat et vivíficat, * dedúcit ad ínferos et redúcit.
<n>2:10</n> Dóminus páuperem facit et ditat, * humíliat et súblevat.
<n>2:11</n> Súscitat de púlvere egénum, * et de stércore élevat páuperem:
<n>2:12</n> Ut sédeat cum princípibus, * et sólium glóriæ téneat.
<n>2:13</n> Dómini enim sunt cárdines terræ, * et pósuit super eos orbem.
<n>2:14</n> Pedes sanctórum suórum servábit, et ímpii in ténebris conticéscent: * quia non in fortitúdine sua roborábitur vir.
<n>2:15</n> Dóminum formidábunt adversárii eius: * et super ipsos in cælis tonábit:
<n>2:16</n> Dóminus iudicábit fines terræ, et dabit impérium regi suo, * et sublimábit cornu Christi sui.
00.563aa80c43:
<n>2:1</n> My heart hath rejoiced in the Lord, * and my horn is exalted in my God:
<n>2:2</n> My mouth is enlarged over my enemies: * because I have joyed in thy salvation.
<n>2:3</n> There is none holy as the Lord is: for there is no other beside thee, * and there is none strong like our God.
<n>2:4</n> Do not multiply to speak lofty things, * boasting:
<n>2:5</n> Let old matters depart from your mouth: for the Lord is a God of all knowledge, * and to him are thoughts prepared.
<n>2:6</n> The bow of the mighty is overcome, * and the weak are girt with strength.
<n>2:7</n> They that were full before have hired out themselves for bread: * and the hungry are filled,
<n>2:8</n> So that the barren hath borne many: * and she that had many children is weakened.
<n>2:9</n> The Lord killeth and maketh alive, * he bringeth down to hell and bringeth back again.
<n>2:10</n> The Lord maketh poor and maketh rich, * he humbleth and he exalteth.
<n>2:11</n> He raiseth up the needy from the dust, * and lifteth up the poor from the dunghill:
<n>2:12</n> That he may sit with princes, * and hold the throne of glory.
<n>2:13</n> For the poles of the earth are the Lord’s, * and upon them he hath set the world.
<n>2:14</n> He will keep the feet of his saints, and the wicked shall be silent in darkness, * because no man shall prevail by his own strength.
<n>2:15</n> The adversaries of the Lord shall fear him: * and upon them shall he thunder in the heavens.
<n>2:16</n> The Lord shall judge the ends of the earth, and he shall give empire to his king, * and shall exalt the horn of his Christ.
00.0bbb41635c:
<n>3:2</n> Dómine, audívi auditiónem tuam, * et tímui.
<n>3:2</n> Dómine, opus tuum, * in médio annórum vivífica illud:
<n>3:2</n> In médio annórum notum fácies: * cum irátus fúeris, misericórdiæ recordáberis.
<n>3:3</n> Deus ab Austro véniet, * et sanctus de monte Pharan:
<n>3:3</n> Opéruit cælos glória eius: * et laudis eius plena est terra.
<n>3:4</n> Splendor eius ut lux erit: * córnua in mánibus eius:
<n>3:4</n> Ibi abscóndita est fortitúdo eius: * ante fáciem eius ibit mors.
<n>3:5</n> Et egrediétur diábolus ante pedes eius. * Stetit, et mensus est terram.
<n>3:6</n> Aspéxit, et dissólvit gentes: * et contríti sunt montes sǽculi.
<n>3:6</n> Incurváti sunt colles mundi, * ab itinéribus æternitátis eius.
<n>3:7</n> Pro iniquitáte vidi tentória Æthiópiæ, * turbabúntur pelles terræ Mádian.
<n>3:8</n> Numquid in flumínibus irátus es, Dómine? * aut in flumínibus furor tuus? vel in mari indignátio tua?
<n>3:8</n> Qui ascéndes super equos tuos: * et quadrígæ tuæ salvátio.
<n>3:9</n> Súscitans suscitábis arcum tuum: * iuraménta tríbubus quæ locútus es.
<n>3:9</n> Flúvios scindes terræ: vidérunt te, et doluérunt montes: * gurges aquárum tránsiit.
<n>3:10</n> Dedit abýssus vocem suam: * altitúdo manus suas levávit.
<n>3:11</n> Sol, et luna stetérunt in habitáculo suo, * in luce sagittárum tuárum, ibunt in splendóre fulgurántis hastæ tuæ.
<n>3:12</n> In frémitu conculcábis terram: * et in furóre obstupefácies gentes.
<n>3:13</n> Egréssus es in salútem pópuli tui: * in salútem cum Christo tuo.
<n>3:13</n> Percussísti caput de domo ímpii: * denudásti fundaméntum eius usque ad collum.
<n>3:14</n> Maledixísti sceptris eius, cápiti bellatórum eius, * veniéntibus ut turbo ad dispergéndum me.
<n>3:14</n> Exsultátio eórum * sicut eius, qui dévorat páuperem in abscóndito.
<n>3:15</n> Viam fecísti in mari equis tuis, * in luto aquárum multárum.
<n>3:16</n> Audívi, et conturbátus est venter meus: * a voce contremuérunt lábia mea.
<n>3:16</n> Ingrediátur putrédo in óssibus meis, * et subter me scáteat.
<n>3:16</n> Ut requiéscam in die tribulatiónis: * ut ascéndam ad pópulum accínctum nostrum.
<n>3:17</n> Ficus enim non florébit: * et non erit germen in víneis.
<n>3:17</n> Mentiétur opus olívæ: * et arva non áfferent cibum.
<n>3:17</n> Abscindétur de ovíli pecus: * et non erit arméntum in præsépibus.
<n>3:18</n> Ego autem in Dómino gaudébo: * et exsultábo in Deo Iesu meo.
<n>3:19</n> Deus Dóminus fortitúdo mea: * et ponet pedes meos quasi cervórum.
<n>3:19</n> Et super excélsa mea dedúcet me victor * in psalmis canéntem.
00.1d80389b52:
<n>3:2</n> O Lord, I have heard thy hearing, * and was afraid.
<n>3:2</n> O Lord, thy work, * in the midst of the years bring it to life:
<n>3:2</n> In the midst of the years thou shalt make it known: * when thou art angry, thou wilt remember mercy.
<n>3:3</n> God will come from the south, * and the holy one from mount Pharan:
<n>3:3</n> His glory covered the heavens, * and the earth is full of his praise.
<n>3:4</n> His brightness shall be as the light: * horns are in his hands:
<n>3:4</n> There is his strength hid: * Death shall go before his face.
<n>3:5</n> And the devil shall go forth before his feet. * He stood and measured the earth.
<n>3:6</n> He beheld, and melted the nations: * and the ancient mountains were crushed to pieces.
<n>3:6</n> The hills of the world were bowed down * by the journeys of his eternity.
<n>3:7</n> I saw the tents of Ethiopia for their iniquity, * the curtains of the land of Madian shall be troubled.
<n>3:8</n> Wast thou angry, O Lord, with the rivers? * or was thy wrath upon the rivers? or thy indignation in the sea?
<n>3:8</n> Who will ride upon thy horses: * and thy chariots are salvation.
<n>3:9</n> Thou wilt surely take up thy bow: * according to the oaths which thou hast spoken to the tribes.
<n>3:9</n> Thou wilt divide the rivers of the earth. The mountains saw thee, and were grieved: * the great body of waters passed away.
<n>3:10</n> The deep put forth its voice: * the deep lifted up its hands.
<n>3:11</n> The sun and the moon stood still in their habitation, * in the light of thy arrows, they shall go in the brightness of thy glittering spear.
<n>3:12</n> In thy anger thou wilt tread the earth under foot: * in thy wrath thou wilt astonish the nations.
<n>3:13</n> Thou wentest forth for the salvation of thy people: * for salvation with thy Christ.
<n>3:13</n> Thou struckest the head of the house of the wicked: * thou hast laid bare his foundation even to the neck.
<n>3:14</n> Thou hast cursed his sceptres, the head of his warriors, * them that came out as a whirlwind to scatter me.
<n>3:14</n> Their joy * was like that of him that devoureth the poor man in secret.
<n>3:15</n> Thou madest a way in the sea for thy horses, * in the mud of many waters.
<n>3:16</n> I have heard and my bowels were troubled: * my lips trembled at the voice.
<n>3:16</n> Let rottenness enter into my bones, * and swarm under me.
<n>3:16</n> That I may rest in the day of tribulation: * that I may go up to our people that are girded.
<n>3:17</n> For the fig tree shall not blossom: * and there shall be no spring in the vines.
<n>3:17</n> The labour of the olive tree shall fail: * and the fields shall yield no food:
<n>3:17</n> The flock shall be cut off from the fold, * and there shall be no herd in the stalls.
<n>3:18</n> But I will rejoice in the Lord: * and I will joy in God my Jesus.
<n>3:19</n> The Lord God is my strength: * and he will make my feet like the feet of harts:
<n>3:19</n> And he the conqueror will lead me upon my high places * singing psalms.
00.2a4a5f7f14:
<n>3:52</n> Benedíctus es, Dómine, Deus patrum nostrórum: * et laudábilis, et gloriósus, et superexaltátus in sǽcula.
<n>3:53</n> Et benedíctum nomen glóriæ tuæ sanctum: * et laudábile, et superexaltátum in ómnibus sǽculis.
<n>3:54</n> Benedíctus es in templo sancto glóriæ tuæ: * et superlaudábilis, et supergloriósus in sǽcula.
<n>3:55</n> Benedíctus es in throno regni tui: * et superlaudábilis, et superexaltátus in sǽcula.
<n>3:56</n> Benedíctus es, qui intuéris abýssos, et sedes super Chérubim: * et laudábilis, et superexaltátus in sǽcula.
<n>3:57</n> Benedíctus es in firmaménto cæli: * et laudábilis, et gloriósus in sǽcula.
<n>3:58</n> Benedícite, ómnia ópera Dómini, Dómino: * laudáte, et superexaltáte eum in sǽcula.
00.ccff8c4bb3:
<n>3:52</n> Blessed art thou, O Lord the God of our fathers: * and worthy to be praised, and glorified, and exalted above all for ever:
<n>3:53</n> And blessed is the holy name of thy glory: * and worthy to be praised, and exalted above all in all ages.
<n>3:54</n> Blessed art thou in the holy temple of thy glory: * and exceedingly to be praised, and exceeding glorious for ever.
<n>3:55</n> Blessed art thou on the throne of thy kingdom, * and exceedingly to be praised, and exalted above all for ever.
<n>3:56</n> Blessed art thou, that beholdest the depths, and sittest upon the cherubims: * and worthy to be praised and exalted above all for ever.
<n>3:57</n> Blessed art thou in the firmament of heaven: * and worthy of praise, and glorious for ever.
<n>3:58</n> All ye works of the Lord, bless the Lord: * praise and exalt him above all for ever.
